sequences.title: Transparent handling of an unknown RR

intro.quote: To enable new RR types to be deployed without server changes, name servers and resolvers MUST handle RRs of unknown type transparently.

steps.explain: The sender treats the RDATA as unstructured binary data and transmits it without change.

cite.quote: To enable new RR types to be deployed without server changes, name servers and resolvers MUST handle RRs of unknown type transparently. That is, they must treat the RDATA section of such RRs as unstructured binary data, storing and transmitting it without change [RFC1123].

intro.quote: To ensure the correct operation of equality comparison (section 6) and of the DNSSEC canonical form (section 7) when an RR type is known to some but not all of the servers involved, servers MUST also exactly preserve the RDATA of RRs of known type, except for changes due to compression or decompression where allowed by section 4 of this memo.

steps.explain: The sender preserves the known-type RDATA exactly, except for compression or decompression changes allowed by the RFC.

cite.quote: To ensure the correct operation of equality comparison (section 6) and of the DNSSEC canonical form (section 7) when an RR type is known to some but not all of the servers involved, servers MUST also exactly preserve the RDATA of RRs of known type, except for changes due to compression or decompression where allowed by section 4 of this memo.

sequences.title: Generic parsing of a known RR type

intro.quote: An implementation MAY also choose to represent some RRs of known type using the above generic representations for the type, class and/or RDATA, which carries the benefit of making the resulting master file portable to servers where these types are unknown.

steps.explain: After generic parsing, the server still treats the record as a known type and applies the applicable compression, canonicalization, and other type-specific rules.

cite.quote: Even though an RR of known type represented in the \# format is effectively treated as an unknown type for the purpose of parsing the RDATA text representation, all further processing by the server MUST treat it as a known type and take into account any applicable type-specific rules regarding compression, canonicalization, etc.

headers.title: Generic class, type, and RDATA representation

intro.quote: This convention allows types and classes to be distinguished from each other and from TTL values, allowing the "[<TTL>] [<class>] <type> <RDATA>" and "[<class>] [<TTL>] <type> <RDATA>" forms of [RFC1035] to both be unambiguously parsed.

fields.name: CLASS
fields.explain: An unknown class is written as CLASS followed by its decimal class number.

cite.quote: In the "class" field, an unknown class is similarly represented as the word "CLASS" immediately followed by the decimal class number.

fields.name: TYPE
fields.explain: An unknown RR type is written as TYPE followed by its decimal type number without intervening whitespace.

cite.quote: In the "type" field of a master file line, an unknown RR type is represented by the word "TYPE" immediately followed by the decimal RR type number, with no intervening whitespace.

fields.name: RDATA
fields.explain: The generic text starts with a marker token, then gives an unsigned decimal octet length, followed by zero or more hexadecimal words with an even number of digits each.

cite.quote: The special token \# (a backslash immediately followed by a hash sign), which identifies the RDATA as having the generic encoding defined herein rather than a traditional type-specific encoding. An unsigned decimal integer specifying the RDATA length in octets. Zero or more words of hexadecimal data encoding the actual RDATA field, each containing an even number of hexadecimal digits.
